title: Exodus 33 — The tent of meeting outside the camp + 'no man shall see me and live'

translation.sourceText: Hebrew Masoretic text (Westminster Leningrad Codex base, Public Domain) — Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra

verdicts.reasoning: lēḵ ʿălēh mizzeh ... nišbaʿtî ... ləzarʿăḵā ʾettənennâ: exact. 'Swore' is exodus-woh's modern register, and 'Mitsrayim' follows the published exodus-woh practice.
wəšālaḥtî ləp̄āneyḵā malʾāḵ 'a messenger' under central malakh-yhwh-messenger (ASV 'an angel'). The six gentilics follow exodus-woh 3:8 (checked).
kî lōʾ ʾeʿĕleh bəqirbəḵā ... pen-ʾăḵelḵā: exact.
haddāḇār hārāʿ hazzeh 'this evil word': literal (ASV). wayyiṯʾabbālû 'they mourned'. Exact.
reḡaʿ ʾeḥāḏ ʾeʿĕleh bəqirbəḵā wəḵillîṯîḵā rendered as a real conditional; defensible (ASV). The nested speech takes single marks.
wayyiṯnaṣṣəlû ... mēhar ḥôrēḇ 'from Mount Horeb onward' (NJPS 'from Mount Horeb on'). Defensible reading of the min.

citations: Haran, Temples and Temple-Service in Ancient Israel (1978)
verdicts.reasoning: The yiqqaḥ ... wənāṭâ sequence is rendered as iterative ('used to take'), which is correct. lô is left unexpressed with the ASV.
Frequentative wəhāyâ ... yāqûmû rendered 'whenever ... would'; exact.

wəḏibber ʿim-mōšeh without an expressed subject is rendered 'he', which preserves the ambiguity (the ASV supplies the divine name). The reception note on TBWTT ch. 3's capitalised 'He' is accurate. No leakage.

citations: Gruber, Aspects of Nonverbal Communication in the Ancient Near East (1980)
verdicts.reasoning: wəqām kol-hāʿām wəhištaḥăwû: 'bow down' (ASV 'worship') under the Torah clause, consistent with 24:1 and exodus-woh 20:5.

citations: Moberly, At the Mountain of God (1983)
verdicts.reasoning: pānîm ʾel-pānîm kaʾăšer yəḏabbēr ʾîš ʾel-rēʿēhû: ASV wording. The reception note (TBWTT ch. 3, 'man to man') is accurate.
Exact; the nested quotations are marked correctly.
hôḏiʿēnî nāʾ ʾeṯ-dərāḵeḵā wəʾēdāʿăḵā ... ûrəʾēh kî ʿamməḵā haggôy hazzeh: exact.

citations: Moberly, At the Mountain of God (1983)
verdicts.reasoning: pānay yēlēḵû 'My presence shall go': the pānîm-as-presence sense (HALOT 'in person'), without the ASV's supplied 'with thee'. Read as a statement, which is defensible.
Exact; 'presence' consistent with v 14.
wənip̄lênû 'so that we are set apart' (plh Niphal) and ʿal-pənê hāʾăḏāmâ 'the face of the earth' (the world idiom) are accurate.
Exact.
harʾēnî nāʾ ʾeṯ-kəḇōḏeḵā: exact; central kavod.
ʾaʿăḇîr kol-ṭûḇî ... wəqārāʾṯî ḇəšēm YHWH ... idem per idem: exact (ASV). Non-blocking citation fix: Lundbom's 'God's Use of the Idem per Idem to Terminate Debate' is in HTR 71 (1978), not VT 28.

lōʾ ṯûḵal lirʾōṯ ʾeṯ-pānāy kî lōʾ-yirʾanî hāʾāḏām wāḥāy: 'man' is the generic article rendered with the ASV. The reception notes on TBWTT ch. 3 (atmosphere, suits) and LWTE ch. 1 are accurate (checked against the canon file), and the line encodes neither reading.
Exact.
bəniqraṯ haṣṣûr ... wəśakkōṯî ḵappî: exact (ASV 'hand').
ʾăḥōrāy 'my back' (ASV, NJPS). The anthropomorphism is left in the line and its later readings are confined to the commentary. Exact.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-proper-names: Option (a) for this wave: keep the split, do not retro-edit signed-off chapters, and record it in the corpus. For the later normalization pass the reviewer recommends one form per name across the corpus. Prefer the transliterated 'Moshe'/'Par'oh', because they are the only English forms left in an otherwise transliterated Torah and the ASV equivalence table already serves readers of the canon's KJV-based English. Prefer the tz spelling 'Mitzrayim', since tz is already the Torah rule for every other tsade. Keep 'the Egyptians' for the population (amend the central gentilic 'Mitsri', which no volume uses), and bring isaiah-woh 'Egypt' into the same decision.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-torah: Retire the transliterated 'torah' at the next Exodus pass and apply the sense rule. Ex 13:9 'the law of YHWH' is a Deuteronomic-style formula (ASV, NRSV 'law'), and Ex 16:4 'my law' (ASV, NRSV) or 'my instruction' (NJPS 'teaching') is a founder preference. Keep Isaiah's 'teaching' as the prophetic clause of the same central entry.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F3-bara: Agree. Keep 'create' outside Gen 1 (Deut 4:32; Isaiah 40-65 already do), and add a scope sentence to central bara saying that 'shape' is the Gen 1 rendering only.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-teruma: Ratify 'oblation' with hērîm 'set apart'. It is lexically sound, already the corpus term in Ezekiel and Isa 40:20, and it removes the unsupported 'heave' etymology. Semver: minor is defensible because no shipped line changes, but renumber the three parallel 2.84.0 diffs sequentially.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-merism: Confirm 'the heavens and the earth' for the merism outside Gen 1 (exodus-woh 20:11; Deut 4:26, 39). State explicitly that the creation formulas of Isaiah ('created the skies', 'spread out the earth') render the physical sky 'skies', so that the two practices read as one rule.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F6-saraf: The Isaiah wave has already applied the same rule ('a fiery flying serpent' at Isa 14:29; 'seraphim' for the Isa 6 attendants). Promote one central śārāp̄ entry stating both clauses.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F7-herem: The Former Prophets decision is now visible ('devoted thing' / 'devote to destruction'). Adopt it at Num 21:2-3 (reviewer revise), promote a single central ḥērem entry, and reconcile isaiah-woh 43:28 'the ban'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F8-deuteronomy-quotation: Confirm. It matches NJPS practice and the chapter applies it consistently (4:6, 10 inner double marks; 4:41 narration). Apply it unchanged to Deut 1-3 and 5.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F9-kapporet: Keep 'mercy-seat' (ASV, NRSV). It preserves the link with kippēr and Lev 16 that 'cover' loses, and the dispute is fully recorded in the commentary.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F10-next-exodus-pass: Agree with all three items (16:16 'souls'; the 'heavens' register check at 16:4; 17:14; 20:4, 11, 19; 13:9 and 16:4 'torah'). Add the FP1 shofar refId correction (EXO-WOH-20:15, not 20:18) to the merge checklist.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֙ לֵ֣ךְ עֲלֵ֣ה מִזֶּ֔ה אַתָּ֣ה וְהָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱלִ֖יתָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֶל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִ֠שְׁבַּעְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֨ם לְיִצְחָ֤ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹב֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְזַרְעֲךָ֖ אֶתְּנֶֽנָּה׃

i18n.en: And YHWH spoke to Moses, "Depart, go up from here, you and the people whom you have brought up out of the land of Mitsrayim, to the land of which I swore to Avraham, to Yitzchaq, and to Ya'aqov, saying, 'To your seed I will give it.'

notes.official: *lēḵ ʿălēh mizzeh* 'Depart, go up from here'. The chapter follows the golden-calf crisis (Ex 32) and turns on whether YHWH himself will go with the people. *ʾăšer nišbaʿtî ləʾaḇrāhām ləyiṣḥāq ûləyaʿăqōḇ* 'which I swore to Avraham, to Yitzchaq, and to Ya'aqov' (central `nishba-la-avraham-le-yitzchaq-u-le-yaaqov-patriarchal-oath-triple-formula-cross-corpus`, whose rationale names this verse); the entry's 'sware' is the ASV register of genesis-woh, and exodus-woh's modern register gives 'swore', recorded in the wave's central diff. *ləzarʿăḵā ʾettənennâ* 'To your seed I will give it' (Gen 12:7). *mēʾereṣ miṣrāyim* 'out of the land of Mitsrayim' (central `mitsrayim`; `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁלַחְתִּ֥י לְפָנֶ֖יךָ מַלְאָ֑ךְ וְגֵֽרַשְׁתִּ֗י אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י וְהַֽחִתִּי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃

i18n.en: And I will send a messenger before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite —

notes.official: *wəšālaḥtî ləp̄āneyḵā malʾāḵ* 'And I will send a messenger before you' (ASV 'an angel'; central `malakh-yhwh-messenger`, whose appliesTo already lists this verse as EXOD-33:2). The messenger stands in for YHWH's own presence (v 3), and the chapter asks whether that substitution will stand (vv 12-17). The six peoples keep exodus-woh's English gentilics (3:8, 17) under `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`; the transliterated forms of the central `ten-nations-of-canaan` are scoped to Gen 15.

paragraphs.text: אֶל־אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָ֑שׁ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א אֶֽעֱלֶ֜ה בְּקִרְבְּךָ֗ כִּ֤י עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֙רֶף֙ אַ֔תָּה פֶּן־אֲכֶלְךָ֖ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃

i18n.en: to a land flowing with milk and honey; for I will not go up in your midst, for you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you on the way."

notes.official: *ʾereṣ zāḇaṯ ḥālāḇ ûḏəḇāš* 'a land flowing with milk and honey' (central `eretz`). *kî ʿam-qəšēh-ʿōrep̄ ʾattâ* 'for you are a stiff-necked people', the image of a draught animal that will not bend its neck to the yoke (32:9; 34:9; Deut 9:6, 13). *pen-ʾăḵelḵā* 'lest I consume you'.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע הָעָ֗ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הָרָ֛ע הַזֶּ֖ה וַיִּתְאַבָּ֑לוּ וְלֹא־שָׁ֛תוּ אִ֥ישׁ עֶדְי֖וֹ עָלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And when the people heard this evil word, they mourned, and no man put his ornaments on him.

notes.official: *haddāḇār hārāʿ hazzeh* 'this evil word', i.e. this bad news. *ʿeḏyô* 'his ornaments'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֱמֹ֤ר אֶל־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אַתֶּ֣ם עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֔רֶף רֶ֧גַע אֶחָ֛ד אֶֽעֱלֶ֥ה בְקִרְבְּךָ֖ וְכִלִּיתִ֑יךָ וְעַתָּ֗ה הוֹרֵ֤ד עֶדְיְךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וְאֵדְעָ֖ה מָ֥ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Moses, "Say to the children of Yisra'el, 'You are a stiff-necked people; if for one moment I were to go up in your midst, I would consume you. And now, take off your ornaments from you, that I may know what to do to you.'"

notes.official: *wəʿattâ hôrēḏ ʿeḏyəḵā mēʿāleyḵā* 'And now, take off your ornaments from you': putting off ornaments is a sign of mourning and contrition, and the ornaments may recall the gold of the calf (32:2-4; Childs 1974). The speech Moses is to deliver is set in single quotation marks inside YHWH's speech (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּֽתְנַצְּל֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־עֶדְיָ֖ם מֵהַ֥ר חוֹרֵֽב׃

i18n.en: And the children of Yisra'el stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb onward.

notes.official: *wayyiṯnaṣṣəlû* 'stripped themselves', the verb used in the Piel for the despoiling of Mitsrayim (3:22; 12:36), here reflexive. *mēhar ḥôrēḇ* 'from Mount Horeb onward' (central `har-sinai-horev-the-mountain-of-Elohim-divine-mountain-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וּמֹשֶׁה֩ יִקַּ֨ח אֶת־הָאֹ֜הֶל וְנָֽטָה־ל֣וֹ ׀ מִח֣וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֗ה הַרְחֵק֙ מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְקָ֥רָא ל֖וֹ אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְהָיָה֙ כָּל־מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה יֵצֵא֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִח֥וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

i18n.en: And Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far off from the camp, and he called it the tent of meeting. And it came to pass that everyone who sought YHWH would go out to the tent of meeting, which was outside the camp.

notes.official: *ûmōšeh yiqqaḥ ʾeṯ-hāʾōhel wənāṭâ-lô* 'And Moses used to take the tent and pitch it': the imperfect and the following perfects with *wə* describe a repeated practice. This tent stands outside the camp and is distinct from the tabernacle of Ex 25-31, which stands at its centre (Num 2:17) (Haran, *Temples and Temple-Service in Ancient Israel*, 1978; Childs 1974). *lô* is either 'for himself' (Rashi) or 'for it', i.e. the ark; the ASV leaves it unexpressed and the line does the same. *ʾōhel môʿēḏ* 'the tent of meeting', as 1-kings-woh 8:4. *kol-məḇaqqēš YHWH* 'everyone who sought YHWH', i.e. who came to consult him.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כְּצֵ֤את מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־הָאֹ֔הֶל יָק֙וּמוּ֙ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם וְנִ֨צְּב֔וּ אִ֖ישׁ פֶּ֣תַח אָהֳל֑וֹ וְהִבִּ֙יטוּ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה עַד־בֹּא֖וֹ הָאֹֽהֱלָה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, whenever Moses went out to the tent, that all the people would rise up and stand, each man at the entrance of his tent, and look after Moses until he had gone into the tent.

notes.official: *wəhibbîṭû ʾaḥărê mōšeh* 'and look after Moses': the people stand at the entrances of their own tents and watch him until he goes in.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כְּבֹ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ הָאֹ֔הֱלָה יֵרֵד֙ עַמּ֣וּד הֶֽעָנָ֔ן וְעָמַ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל וְדִבֶּ֖ר עִם־מֹשֶֽׁה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, whenever Moses entered the tent, that the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent, and he would speak with Moses.

notes.official:
*yērēḏ ʿammûḏ heʿānān wəʿāmaḏ petaḥ hāʾōhel* 'the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent' (central `pillar-of-cloud-and-fire-ammud-ha-anan-ve-esh-divine-presence-marker-cross-corpus`). In this tradition the cloud comes down to the tent when Moses enters, whereas in the Priestly texts it rests on the tabernacle (40:34-38; Num 9:15-23). *wəḏibber ʿim-mōšeh* 'and he would speak with Moses': the verb has no expressed subject. The nearest masculine noun is *ʿammûḏ* 'pillar', v 11 names YHWH as the speaker, and the ASV supplies '[Jehovah]'; the line leaves the subject as unexpressed as the Hebrew does, with the English pronoun 'he'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('And it came to pass, as Moses entered into the tent, the cloudy pillar descended, and stood at the door of the tent. And He talked with Moses'), with the phrase 'He would enter into the tent of meeting', in its account of the tent as the place where the creators met the representatives of men. The canon's capitalised 'He' supplies the subject the Hebrew leaves open. The line keeps the Hebrew's ambiguity and renders *ʿammûḏ heʿānān* under the central entry.

paragraphs.text: וְרָאָ֤ה כָל־הָעָם֙ אֶת־עַמּ֣וּד הֶֽעָנָ֔ן עֹמֵ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל וְקָ֤ם כָּל־הָעָם֙ וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוּ֔וּ אִ֖ישׁ פֶּ֥תַח אָהֳלֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And all the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, and all the people would rise up and bow down, each man at the entrance of his tent.

notes.official: *wəqām kol-hāʿām wəhištaḥăwû ʾîš petaḥ ʾohŏlô* 'and all the people would rise up and bow down, each man at the entrance of his tent' (draft and ASV 'worship'): the people prostrate themselves at a distance, toward the pillar. 'Bow down' follows the Torah clause of the central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship`, as at 24:1 and exodus-woh 20:5. Pillar of cloud: central `pillar-of-cloud-and-fire-ammud-ha-anan-ve-esh-divine-presence-marker-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: וְדִבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֙ פָּנִ֣ים אֶל־פָּנִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְדַבֵּ֥ר אִ֖ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְשָׁב֙ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וּמְשָׁ֨רְת֜וֹ יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ בִּן־נוּן֙ נַ֔עַר לֹ֥א יָמִ֖ישׁ מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֹֽהֶל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And YHWH would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. And he would return to the camp; but his attendant Yehoshua the son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from the midst of the tent.

notes.official:
*wəḏibber YHWH ʾel-mōšeh pānîm ʾel-pānîm kaʾăšer yəḏabbēr ʾîš ʾel-rēʿēhû* 'And YHWH would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend' (central `peniel-panim-el-panim-divine-face-encounter`). The formula describes the directness of the communication (cf. Num 12:8 *peh ʾel-peh* 'mouth to mouth'; Deut 34:10), while v 20 states that YHWH's face cannot be seen. The central entry records the main resolutions of the tension (a metaphor of intimacy; different sources; a distinction between speaking and seeing) without choosing among them (Moberly, *At the Mountain of God*, 1983). *ûməšārəṯô yəhôšuaʿ bin-nûn naʿar* 'but his attendant Yehoshua the son of Nun, a young man' (as 24:13) stays in the tent when Moses returns to the camp.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('And Yahweh spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend') and compares it with the conversation between the creator and Raël, 'man to man'. The line renders the idiom as the ASV and the central entry do.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־יְהוָ֗ה רְ֠אֵה אַתָּ֞ה אֹמֵ֤ר אֵלַי֙ הַ֚עַל אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאַתָּה֙ לֹ֣א הֽוֹדַעְתַּ֔נִי אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־תִּשְׁלַ֖ח עִמִּ֑י וְאַתָּ֤ה אָמַ֙רְתָּ֙ יְדַעְתִּ֣יךָֽ בְשֵׁ֔ם וְגַם־מָצָ֥אתָ חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָֽי׃

i18n.en: And Moses said to YHWH, "See, you say to me, 'Bring up this people,' but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, 'I know you by name, and you have also found favor in my sight.'

notes.official: Moses' intercession (vv 12-17) turns on the verb *yḏʿ* 'know': 'you have not let me know whom you will send with me' (cf. the messenger of v 2), and *yəḏaʿtîḵā ḇəšēm* 'I know you by name', a formula of choice and intimacy (v 17). *māṣāʾṯā ḥēn bəʿênāy* 'you have found favor in my sight' (central `matza-chen-be-einei-x-favor-formula`). The quoted words of YHWH take single marks inside Moses' speech.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה אִם־נָא֩ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֜ן בְּעֵינֶ֗יךָ הוֹדִעֵ֤נִי נָא֙ אֶת־דְּרָכֶ֔ךָ וְאֵדָ֣עֲךָ֔ לְמַ֥עַן אֶמְצָא־חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וּרְאֵ֕ה כִּ֥י עַמְּךָ֖ הַגּ֥וֹי הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And now, if I have found favor in your sight, show me now your ways, that I may know you, so that I may find favor in your sight; and consider that this nation is your people."

notes.official: *hôḏiʿēnî nāʾ ʾeṯ-dərāḵeḵā* 'show me now your ways': the request concerns YHWH's intentions and conduct, and 34:6-7 answers it with the list of the divine attributes (cf. Ps 103:7 'he made known his ways to Moses'). *ûrəʾēh kî ʿamməḵā haggôy hazzeh* 'and consider that this nation is your people', answering YHWH's 'your people, whom you brought up' (32:7). Central `matza-chen-be-einei-x-favor-formula`.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר פָּנַ֥י יֵלֵ֖כוּ וַהֲנִחֹ֥תִי לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And he said, "My presence shall go, and I will give you rest."

notes.official: *pānay yēlēḵû wahăniḥōṯî lāḵ* 'My presence shall go, and I will give you rest'. *pānay* is literally 'my face', with a plural verb; with a verb of going it denotes YHWH's own presence, and the line follows the ASV 'presence' without its supplied 'with thee' (`panim-presence-face-convention-torah`; NJPS 'I will go in the lead'; HALOT *pānîm* 6 'in person'). The word runs through the chapter (vv 11, 14, 15, 16, 19, 20, 23). *wahăniḥōṯî lāḵ* 'I will give you rest', i.e. bring you to a settled land (Deut 3:20; 12:9-10). The verse is sometimes read as a question ('Must my presence go?'), but nothing in the Hebrew marks it as one (Moberly 1983).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑יו אִם־אֵ֤ין פָּנֶ֙יךָ֙ הֹלְכִ֔ים אַֽל־תַּעֲלֵ֖נוּ מִזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And he said to him, "If your presence does not go, do not bring us up from here.

notes.official: *ʾim-ʾên pāneyḵā hōləḵîm* 'If your presence does not go' (`panim-presence-face-convention-torah`): Moses takes up the word of v 14 and makes YHWH's own presence the condition of the journey.

paragraphs.text: וּבַמֶּ֣ה ׀ יִוָּדַ֣ע אֵפ֗וֹא כִּֽי־מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲנִ֣י וְעַמֶּ֔ךָ הֲל֖וֹא בְּלֶכְתְּךָ֣ עִמָּ֑נוּ וְנִפְלֵ֙ינוּ֙ אֲנִ֣י וְעַמְּךָ֔ מִכָּ֨ל־הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: For how then shall it be known that I have found favor in your sight, I and your people? Is it not in your going with us, so that we are set apart, I and your people, from all the people that are upon the face of the earth?"

notes.official: *wənip̄lênû ʾănî wəʿamməḵā* 'so that we are set apart, I and your people' (ASV 'separated'): *plh* (Niphal) 'be distinct, distinguished' (cf. 8:18 MT; 9:4; 11:7). *ʿal-pənê hāʾăḏāmâ* 'upon the face of the earth', the idiom for the inhabited world; 'earth' under `adamah-earth-land-ground-scope-torah`. The verse has the chapter's word *pānîm* once more. Central `matza-chen-be-einei-x-favor-formula`.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה גַּ֣ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֑ה כִּֽי־מָצָ֤אתָ חֵן֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י וָאֵדָעֲךָ֖ בְּשֵֽׁם׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Moses, "This thing also that you have spoken I will do; for you have found favor in my sight, and I know you by name."

notes.official: *gam ʾeṯ-haddāḇār hazzeh ʾăšer dibbartā ʾeʿĕśeh* 'This thing also that you have spoken I will do': YHWH grants that his presence will go. 'I know you by name' as v 12 (central `matza-chen-be-einei-x-favor-formula`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַרְאֵ֥נִי נָ֖א אֶת־כְּבֹדֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And he said, "Show me, I pray, your glory."

notes.official: *harʾēnî nāʾ ʾeṯ-kəḇōḏeḵā* 'Show me, I pray, your glory' (central `kavod-yhwh`, here in direct address; NJPS 'your Presence'). The request goes beyond the presence granted in v 17 to a sight of the *kāḇôḏ*, which the following verses partly refuse.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֲנִ֨י אַעֲבִ֤יר כָּל־טוּבִי֙ עַל־פָּנֶ֔יךָ וְקָרָ֧אתִֽי בְשֵׁ֛ם יְהוָ֖ה לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְחַנֹּתִי֙ אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָחֹ֔ן וְרִחַמְתִּ֖י אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲרַחֵֽם׃

i18n.en: And he said, "I will make all my goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of YHWH before you; and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy."

notes.official: *ʾănî ʾaʿăḇîr kol-ṭûḇî ʿal-pāneyḵā* 'I will make all my goodness pass before you': YHWH substitutes his 'goodness' for the glory, and 'before you' is literally 'before your face'. *wəqārāʾṯî ḇəšēm YHWH ləp̄āneyḵā* 'and I will proclaim the name of YHWH before you' (ASV): the subject is YHWH himself, so the central `qara-b-shem-yhwh` ('called on the name', of human worship) does not apply; the proclamation is carried out at 34:5-7. *wəḥannōṯî ʾeṯ-ʾăšer ʾāḥōn wəriḥamtî ʾeṯ-ʾăšer ʾăraḥēm* 'I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy': the *idem per idem* construction of 3:14 (*ʾehyeh ʾăšer ʾehyeh*), which asserts the freedom of the subject (Lundbom, *VT* 28, 1978); quoted at Rom 9:15.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹ֥א תוּכַ֖ל לִרְאֹ֣ת אֶת־פָּנָ֑י כִּ֛י לֹֽא־יִרְאַ֥נִי הָאָדָ֖ם וָחָֽי׃

i18n.en: And he said, "You cannot see my face, for man shall not see me and live."

notes.official:
*lōʾ ṯûḵal lirʾōṯ ʾeṯ-pānāy kî lōʾ-yirʾanî hāʾāḏām wāḥāy* 'You cannot see my face, for man shall not see me and live'. *hāʾāḏām* has the generic article ('the human being', anyone); the line keeps the ASV's generic 'man' (NRSV 'no one'), since the central `ha-adam` 'the human' is scoped to the creature of Gen 2. The statement belongs to the wider belief that the sight of the deity is lethal (Gen 32:31; Judg 6:22-23; 13:22; Isa 6:5), which v 11 and 24:10-11 qualify (central `peniel-panim-el-panim-divine-face-encounter`). *pānay* 'my face' is here the visible face (`panim-presence-face-convention-torah`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live!') and reads it as an allusion to the difference between the atmospheres of the creators' planet and of Earth: on Earth the creators can be seen only in protective suits, and a man on their planet would see them without suits but would die. *Let's Welcome the Extraterrestrials* (ch. 1) returns to the verse when answering an apparent contradiction between the first and second messages. The line renders the Hebrew as the ASV does and encodes neither reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֥ה מָק֖וֹם אִתִּ֑י וְנִצַּבְתָּ֖ עַל־הַצּֽוּר׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said, "Behold, there is a place by me, and you shall stand upon the rock.

notes.official: *hinnēh māqôm ʾittî* 'Behold, there is a place by me': *māqôm* 'place' is also a term for a holy site (Gen 22:3-4; 28:11). *wəniṣṣaḇtā ʿal-haṣṣûr* 'and you shall stand upon the rock', as at Horeb (17:6). Eliyahu's experience at Horeb (1 Kgs 19:9-13) is modelled on this scene.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֙ בַּעֲבֹ֣ר כְּבֹדִ֔י וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךָ בְּנִקְרַ֣ת הַצּ֑וּר וְשַׂכֹּתִ֥י כַפִּ֛י עָלֶ֖יךָ עַד־עָבְרִֽי׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass, while my glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft of the rock, and I will cover you with my hand until I have passed by.

notes.official: *bəniqraṯ haṣṣûr* 'in a cleft of the rock'. *wəśakkōṯî ḵappî ʿāleyḵā* 'and I will cover you with my hand': *kap̄* is the palm or hollow of the hand, and the ASV 'hand' is kept. *kəḇōḏî* 'my glory' (central `kavod-yhwh`).

paragraphs.text: וַהֲסִרֹתִי֙ אֶת־כַּפִּ֔י וְרָאִ֖יתָ אֶת־אֲחֹרָ֑י וּפָנַ֖י לֹ֥א יֵרָאֽוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And I will take away my hand, and you shall see my back; but my face shall not be seen."

notes.official: *wərāʾîṯā ʾeṯ-ʾăḥōrāy ûp̄ānay lōʾ yērāʾû* 'and you shall see my back; but my face shall not be seen'. *ʾăḥōrayim* is the back or hinder side (26:12; 1 Kgs 7:25), and 'my back' is the ASV and NJPS rendering. The anthropomorphism is the text's own; Jewish and Christian interpreters have read it as 'what comes after me', the traces of YHWH's passing or his deeds (b. Berakhot 7a; Maimonides, *Guide* 1.38; Gregory of Nyssa, *Life of Moses* 2.219-255). The line renders the noun. *ûp̄ānay lōʾ yērāʾû* has a plural verb with *pānîm* (`panim-presence-face-convention-torah`).
